Subject: Initial ask — connecting Legato VPC to Redwood Private deployment

Thanks for taking this. We're evaluating Redwood Private for hosting an inference endpoint for a regulated payments workflow. Can you lay out the recommended approaches to connect our AWS VPC to a Redwood Private deployment (we're currently running in us-west-2)? High level we care about:

- Security & auditability (SOC2 constraints)
- Low predictable latency (p95 target < 40ms)
- Operational simplicity for our NetOps team
- Cost sensitivity for sustained traffic ~15k req/day

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Todd Ramos <todd.ramos@legato.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — connecting Legato VPC to Redwood Private deployment

Todd —

Appreciate the diagram and the clarity on constraints. High-level options we typically present (short summary; I'll bring detailed cost/latency numbers to the call):

1) VPC Peering
- Pros: Low latency, straightforward routing (private IPs). Good for high-throughput, stable links.
- Cons: Cross-account peering scales poorly across many prefixes; requires routing maintenance for multi-region setups; no AWS-managed endpoint — firewall exposure depends on your NAT/IGW configs.

2) AWS PrivateLink (interface VPC Endpoint to our Endpoint Service)
- Pros: Strong isolation (no route table changes on your side), explicit IAM controls for the endpoint service, better fit for least-privilege and auditability. Easy to restrict to specific ENIs.
- Cons: Per-GB data processing costs and per-hours ENI costs; can add a few ms of latency vs peering depending on topology.

3) Site-to-Site (S2S) VPN
- Pros: Quick to set up as a fallback, good for bursty or lower-cost proof-of-concept. Encrypted in transit.
- Cons: Higher latency/jitter and not ideal for predictable p95 SLAs at scale; maintenance overhead for tunnels.

Recommendation approach for Legato: run a short PoC with PrivateLink to validate security/observability and confirm p95. If latency or cost doesn't meet targets, we run a peering pilot for a subset of subnets as a higher-throughput path and keep PrivateLink as the controlled IAM-first route. We usually advise S2S VPN only as temporary or DR fallback.

Can you confirm: expected avg payload size per request, whether keep-alive TCP connections are acceptable, and whether you have a dedicated cross-account CIDR plan or will use NAT? That'll help us pick exact configs.

I'm copying Ben (network lead) and Kimberly (security) so we can coordinate the technical deep-dive. Attaching a short cheatsheet that compares costs/latency at a glance.

Attachments: redwood-connection-options-cheatsheet.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — available most of next week for the call.

—Marissa
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, Todd Ramos <todd.ramos@legato.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — connecting Legato VPC to Redwood Private deployment

Todd / team —

Quick numbers from our infra bench for the options Marissa outlined (ballpark for us-west-2):

- VPC Peering: median added latency ~1–3ms; 95th up to ~12ms depending on cross-AZ hops. Cost: routing only (no per-GB charge aside from standard data transfer inter-AZ/region).
- PrivateLink: median added latency ~4–8ms; 95th up to ~20ms. Cost: ENI-hour + per-GB processing (AWS). For 15k req/day with avg 12KB payloads, estimate ~$900–$1,400/month in AWS charges for the endpoint depending on concurrency and ENI count.
- S2S VPN: median added latency ~15–40ms; jitter higher. Managed VPN appliances can reduce jitter but cost/ops higher.

Operational note: if you use long-lived TCP connections with Keep-Alive, PrivateLink gives better connection reuse semantics vs S2S. If your traffic is short bursts with many new TCP handshakes, peering tends to be more efficient.

I recommend we include a quick perf test during the PoC (iperf3 + synthetic gen at production qps) and gather p50/p95/p99 and also per-GB billing samples.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Todd Ramos <todd.ramos@legato.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 10:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — connecting Legato VPC to Redwood Private deployment

Todd —

A couple security/controls items we'll need to validate as part of the design review:

- KMS/HSM integration: do you require customer-managed keys for encryption in transit termination or are AWS-managed KMS keys acceptable? PrivateLink simplifies KMS scoping for service-to-service traffic.
- Audit logs: we need NAT/flow logs, VPC Endpoint logs, and a copy of your CloudTrail for any cross-account actions for at least 90 days (SOC2 expectation).
- IP allowlists vs mutual-TLS: PrivateLink gives us the ability to rely on ENI-level controls and IAM policies; peering requires tight route and security group discipline.
- Breakglass/incident playbook: if an endpoint is compromised, what's your escalation path? We'll want runbooks for isolated failover to a hardened peered path.

I've attached a short security checklist tailored for Private deployments. Please confirm the compliance window for logs and whether you have a KMS boundary.

Attachments: legato-security-eval.pdf (pdf)

—Kimberly
Head of Security Compliance — Redwood Inference
